sources.name: DMN official meteorological data request
sources.use: Historical station precipitation, temperature, humidity and wind; local calibration of satellite rainfall
sources.caveat: Not a general open API; fees/terms and station completeness may apply.

sources.name: DMN public portal and bulletin/download archive
sources.use: Operational forecasts, warnings, climate reports and station-network context
sources.caveat: Pages/files can change; archive issue time, validity window, checksum and source URL.

sources.name: ONACC climate bulletin library
sources.provider: Observatoire National sur les Changements Climatiques
sources.use: Dekadal alerts, seasonal forecasts, flood/landslide risk language, geography and validity periods
sources.caveat: Forecast/alert evidence, not observed inundation. Some downloads may require account/session.

sources.name: ONACC Data, Modelling & Geomatics
sources.access: Web catalogue / downloadable layers / described target architecture
sources.use: Flood-risk layers, vulnerability layers, Sentinel/GPM/CHIRPS methodology, hydrological/hydraulic model leads, Far North pilots
sources.caveat: The page describes some future/target database and web-service capabilities; verify every endpoint before treating it as operational.

sources.name: Direction de la Protection Civile
sources.use: Official disaster-response authority, event validation, emergency planning, field/impact data partnership
sources.caveat: Detailed incident database is not exposed as a public machine feed.

sources.name: MINAT Far North flood and Maga infrastructure notices
sources.use: Official emergency chronology, dike/reservoir degradation, field inspections and response actions
sources.caveat: Search/archive documents by date and preserve exact source page.

sources.name: Institut National de la Statistique
sources.use: Population, socioeconomic indicators, regional statistical yearbooks, exposure/vulnerability calibration
sources.caveat: Administrative totals are controls, not gridded flood exposure.

sources.name: INS environment/extreme-event statistics
sources.use: Official/national statistics on environment, hazards and disaster impacts
sources.caveat: Often report-based and temporally aggregated; reconcile with event-level sources.

sources.name: Ministry of Water and Energy
sources.use: Water-resource governance, dams/reservoir projects, emergency plans and infrastructure metadata
sources.caveat: Operational hydrometric data may require institutional access.

sources.name: MINHDU Mbankolo disaster record
sources.use: Grounded causal evidence for 8 Oct 2023: heavy rain + upstream dike/lake failure + houses on drainage path
sources.caveat: Event narrative, not hydrological telemetry; casualty numbers were provisional at publication.

sources.name: MINHDU Yaoundé flood/drainage interventions
sources.use: Drainage bottlenecks, waste blockage, channel/outfall constraints, retention-basin interventions
sources.caveat: Project descriptions need GIS/engineering drawings from partners for quantitative capacity modelling.

sources.name: PCADY / Yaoundé sanitation and flood-control project
sources.use: Retention basins, concrete drainage channels, flood-prevention and alert-system infrastructure
sources.caveat: Extract versioned engineering geometry where available; project status changes over time.

sources.name: Douala stormwater drainage project
sources.use: 39 km drainage canals on nine natural watercourses; urban flood-causal/infrastructure history
sources.caveat: Project-era engineering context is not equivalent to current drain condition/maintenance state.

sources.name: PLIDY integrated flood-risk program
sources.use: Gray/green drainage, solid waste, meteorological services, urban resilience and ongoing infrastructure changes
sources.caveat: Started 2024; model must version infrastructure state rather than assume completed works.

sources.name: Flood Management in the Far North / PULCI
sources.use: 2012 impacts; 70 km Logone dyke, 27 km Maga dam rehabilitation; contingency planning; hydromet network context
sources.caveat: Critical historical infrastructure-state source, not a live feed.

sources.name: Cameroon Flood Emergency Project documents
sources.use: Engineering/environmental details for Logone dyke, Maga dam, irrigation and flood-risk project
sources.caveat: Large PDFs; extract tables/maps with page-level provenance.

sources.name: Lagdo flood-management releases
sources.use: Release start dates, qualitative reservoir management and downstream-warning context; 2024 first releases on 18 Sep
sources.caveat: No verified public continuous numeric telemetry API.

sources.name: Lagdo 2022 reservoir filling/release notice
sources.use: 2022 reservoir filling (91%) and controlled release context driven by rainfall
sources.caveat: Single operational notice, not a time series.

sources.name: SMART rainfall monitoring and alert
sources.use: 15-minute high-resolution rainfall maps from telecom links and integration into flood models/EWS
sources.caveat: Pilot/raw data availability for reuse is not guaranteed; partnership lead.

sources.name: Open Cities Ngaoundéré / Risk Atlas
sources.use: 300+ km² participatory/drone mapping, buildings-at-risk, drainage and waste/blockage context
sources.caveat: Locate/download the latest underlying atlas datasets before production use.

sources.name: UNDRR Cameroon cities flood-risk history
sources.use: Historical recurrence seed: >130 Yaoundé floods 1980–2014; >300 Douala floods over ~3 decades; 2015 urban impacts
sources.caveat: Aggregate city-council figures; do not treat each count as individually geocoded event records.

sources.name: UNDRR Yaoundé VI recurrent flood profile
sources.use: Lowland/wetland/hillside vulnerability, recurrent seasonal flooding and settlement exposure
sources.caveat: Narrative/community profile, not a sensor feed.

sources.name: Cameroon Floods MDRCM039
sources.use: 2024 event chronology, affected population, infrastructure/school/agriculture/livestock impacts and response
sources.caveat: Impact numbers evolve between updates; version by report date.

sources.name: IFRC Cameroon appeals/DREF archive
sources.use: Pouss 2010, MDRCM034 2023 floods, MDRCM039 2024, MDRCM044 2026 Flood EAP and reports
sources.caveat: Keep operation code + report version; an EAP is anticipatory action, not proof a flood occurred.

sources.name: ReliefWeb API v2
sources.use: Cameroon report/disaster search, chronology, source documents and GLIDE/event linking
sources.caveat: API appname/usage rules apply; underlying report copyrights remain.

sources.name: UNFPA Buea 18 March 2023 rapid assessment
sources.use: Exact flash-flood/mudslide event, 2 deaths, >1,100 homeless, water/latrine/pipeline and vulnerability impacts
sources.caveat: Humanitarian rapid assessment; photos/content are copyrighted unless permission/license states otherwise.

sources.name: CEMS EMSN082 Far North 2020
sources.use: Flood delineation/depth and geospatial labels for September 2020 event
sources.caveat: Activation-specific product; preserve AOI/product IDs, source imagery and acquisition time.

sources.name: CEMS EMSR779 Cameroon flood 2024
sources.use: Observed 2024 flood extent and emergency mapping
sources.caveat: Event snapshot(s), not continuous local depth telemetry.

sources.name: International Charter — North Cameroon 2012
sources.provider: International Charter Space and Major Disasters
sources.use: 2012 rainfall + Lagdo release + Benue overflow history; reference/delineation maps
sources.caveat: Separate Benue/Lagdo component from Logone/Maga floodplain component when modelling.

sources.name: International Charter — Far North 2019
sources.provider: International Charter Space and Major Disasters
sources.use: ~100k affected context, Logone overflow chronology, flood/water extent products
sources.caveat: Reported impacts need cross-source reconciliation; maps are acquisition-time specific.

sources.name: International Charter — Western Cameroon 2020
sources.provider: International Charter Space and Major Disasters
sources.use: 2020 urban/western flood footprint; ~900 families displaced; roads/homes/bridge impacts
sources.caveat: Use map product geometry as event observation, not generic city flood hazard.

sources.name: Lake Chad Information System (LIS)
sources.coverage: Lake Chad Basin incl. Logone/Chari Cameroon
sources.use: Historical/up-to-date water, climate, environment and socioeconomic basin data; regional hydrology context
sources.caveat: Dataset download/API permissions vary; record source/vintage and contact LCBC for raw data where needed.

sources.name: LCBC Annual Monitoring Reports
sources.use: Hydrological-year monitoring, basin water/climate observations and historical context
sources.caveat: Report-driven; extract station names/measurements with page-level provenance.

sources.name: VIVA Logone hydrometeorological station program
sources.use: Inventory/georeferencing and deployment of hydrometric, meteorological and groundwater stations in Logone basin
sources.caveat: Public page describes the network; continuous raw sensor feed was not verified publicly.

sources.name: Copernicus Marine sea-level reanalysis
sources.use: 1993+ sea-level anomaly/absolute dynamic topography context for Douala/Limbe compound flooding
sources.caveat: 0.125° offshore product is regional context, not street-scale tide/storm-surge inundation.

sources.name: Copernicus Marine global wave reanalysis
sources.use: 3-hourly wave history (1980+) for coastal/compound flood reconstruction
sources.caveat: Offshore wave model; nearshore transformation and local tide/outfall state remain necessary.

sources.name: Cameroon Water Security Program
sources.use: Institutional/water-resource-management modernization and future partnership/data-infrastructure context
sources.caveat: Program-level source, not an event feed.

sources.name: CAMWATER network/incident information
sources.use: Water-supply asset outages, pipe failures, service vulnerability and recovery after floods
sources.caveat: Not flood hazard data; use only as critical-infrastructure exposure/impact evidence.

sources.name: NASA GPM IMERG Early/Late/Final
sources.access: Earthdata/GES DISC/PPS; HDF5, NetCDF, GeoTIFF, OPeNDAP
sources.use: 30-min rainfall, 1/3/6/12/24/72h accumulations, event trigger and historical reconstruction
sources.caveat: ~0.1°/10 km; never present as street-scale rainfall truth. Early has lowest latency, Final best for retrospective work.

sources.name: CHIRPS v3
sources.use: Historical rainfall climatology, percentiles, antecedent rainfall and event reconstruction at ~0.05°
sources.caveat: Gauge density varies; use local stations where available for calibration.

sources.name: CHIRPS-GEFS
sources.use: Bias-corrected 1–16 day rainfall forecast at ~0.05° for early-warning features
sources.caveat: Forecast uncertainty grows with lead time; preserve ensemble/forecast issue time where available.

sources.name: TAMSAT
sources.use: African rainfall history/monitoring and soil-moisture-related products; independent cross-check
sources.caveat: Use as an independent signal, not automatic replacement for national stations.

sources.name: ERA5-Land
sources.use: Hourly soil/land variables, antecedent wetness, runoff-related context, long historical baselines
sources.caveat: Native ~9 km; reanalysis is modeled/assimilated history, not local sensor truth.

sources.name: SMAP L4
sources.use: Surface/root-zone soil moisture cross-check for catchment wetness
sources.caveat: ~9 km for L4; latency/coverage/quality flags must be preserved.

sources.name: ECMWF Open Data IFS/AIFS
sources.use: Operational precipitation and atmospheric forecast driver
sources.caveat: Forecast grids are regional-scale signals; pin model cycle/issue time and preserve ensemble uncertainty.

sources.name: GloFAS historical
sources.use: Historical discharge, runoff, root-zone soil wetness; percentiles and event reconstruction
sources.caveat: Modeled hydrology; validate locally where gauges exist.

sources.name: GloFAS forecast
sources.use: Forecast river discharge and flood threshold exceedance for riverine early warning
sources.caveat: Not for street-level pluvial floods; preserve ensemble probabilities/issue time.

sources.name: Google Flood Forecasting API
sources.use: Gauges, forecasts, flood status, significant events, serialized inundation polygons; flash-flood search resource
sources.caveat: Access requires approval/API key; gauge coverage must be tested for GH/CM, and gauges can be added/removed.

sources.name: Google Inundation History / GRRR
sources.access: Public historical datasets referenced by Flood Forecasting docs
sources.use: Historical inundation occurrence 1999–2020 and runoff reanalysis/reforecast 1980–2023
sources.caveat: Use as historical evidence; inspect dataset-specific methodology/license before redistribution.

sources.name: Copernicus Global Flood Monitoring (GFM)
sources.access: WMS, Web Push, REST APIs, download UI
sources.use: Observed Sentinel-1 flood extent; automated confirmation layer
sources.caveat: SAR has urban/vegetation/geometry limitations; retain uncertainty/advisory layers and acquisition time.

sources.name: Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping
sources.access: Public JSON API + downloadable mapping products
sources.use: Authoritative event activation metadata and delineation/grading products when activated
sources.caveat: Coverage is activation-based, not every flood. Query first, fall back to own Sentinel/GFM pipeline.

sources.name: Sentinel-1 GRD via Copernicus Data Space
sources.access: STAC, OData/S3, Sentinel Hub Catalog/Process APIs
sources.use: SAR pre/post flood detection, cloud-independent flood mapping
sources.caveat: Requires preprocessing choices; dense urban/flooded vegetation can be difficult; avoid overclaiming.

sources.name: Sentinel-2 L2A via Copernicus Data Space
sources.use: Optical water indices, land cover, before/after visual confirmation
sources.caveat: Clouds are a major limitation during storms; use as supporting evidence, not sole flood sensor.

sources.name: JRC Global Surface Water
sources.use: Permanent/seasonal water mask, occurrence, seasonality, recurrence; isolate new inundation
sources.caveat: Historical product; not a real-time flood feed.

sources.name: JRC Global River Flood Hazard Maps
sources.use: Return-period flood-depth baseline for susceptibility/exposure scenario analysis
sources.caveat: JRC warns these are not official local flood-hazard maps; do not present as local statutory maps.

sources.name: UNOSAT flood products / FloodAI
sources.access: Product catalogue / ArcGIS services / downloadable SHP/GDB/XLS/PDF
sources.use: Independent satellite flood extents and impact products for event validation
sources.caveat: Event availability varies; automated SAR mapping can underestimate water under vegetation/urban conditions.

sources.name: Global Flood Database v1
sources.use: MODIS flood extent/duration labels for historical/event ML features
sources.caveat: 250 m and noncommercial license; not adequate for street-level exposure, but useful for history/training.

sources.name: Sen1Floods11
sources.use: Sentinel-1 flood segmentation training/benchmark
sources.caveat: Research benchmark distribution and domain shift; do not assume Ghana/Cameroon accuracy without validation.

sources.name: SpaceNet 8
sources.use: Flooded roads/buildings segmentation and infrastructure impact model benchmarking
sources.caveat: Benchmark geographies differ from GH/CM; use for transfer-learning experiments, not ground truth in target countries.

sources.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30
sources.use: Elevation, slope, depressions, HAND derivation, drainage conditioning
sources.caveat: DSM artifacts/buildings/vegetation may matter; access conditions for 30 m services should be checked at deployment.

sources.name: HydroSHEDS core
sources.use: Flow direction, flow accumulation, conditioned DEM, flow length
sources.caveat: Some core layers are legacy v1; document product version and resolution.

sources.name: HydroBASINS
sources.use: Catchment/sub-catchment IDs and upstream aggregation units
sources.caveat: Administrative and hydrological units differ; never aggregate rainfall by admin unit when catchment is needed.

sources.name: HydroRIVERS
sources.use: River network, distance-to-river, downstream tracing
sources.caveat: Validate local channels/drains against OSM/national data in urban areas.

sources.name: HydroATLAS
sources.use: Precomputed basin/river attributes: hydrology, climate, land cover, soils, anthropogenic influences
sources.caveat: Useful baseline/context; source vintages vary by attribute.

sources.name: SoilGrids 250 m
sources.use: Clay/sand/silt/organic carbon/bulk density etc. for infiltration/runoff susceptibility
sources.caveat: REST API is currently unreliable/paused; use WCS/WebDAV. Global model not recommended for fine local/farm claims.

sources.name: Dynamic World
sources.use: 10 m built/water/vegetation/crops probabilities; urbanization and impervious proxy changes
sources.caveat: Probabilistic class product; cloud dependence and class uncertainty require temporal compositing/thresholds.

sources.name: ESA WorldCover
sources.use: 10 m land-cover baseline and independent cross-check
sources.caveat: Only specific baseline years; do not call it current land cover.

sources.name: Copernicus Land Cover/Land Use Mapping (LCFM)
sources.use: Newer annual 10 m land-cover information where available
sources.caveat: Check product edition, temporal coverage and regional availability before production.

sources.name: WorldPop Global2 / API v2
sources.use: 100 m population and age/sex exposure inside polygons
sources.caveat: Modeled distribution; cross-check against official census and GHSL; preserve model year.

sources.name: GHSL GHS-POP
sources.use: Independent gridded population exposure and historical urbanization baseline
sources.caveat: Modeled grid; use as cross-check, not exact headcount.

sources.name: GHSL built-up products
sources.use: Built-up surface/volume, settlement structure, urbanization
sources.caveat: Resolution/product vintage varies; useful for aggregate exposure and long-term change.

sources.name: Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints
sources.use: Building-level exposure when OSM buildings are incomplete
sources.caveat: ML-extracted footprints have false positives/omissions and imagery vintage differences; retain confidence/vintage where provided.

sources.name: Microsoft Building Density & Height
sources.use: Built density/height change and urbanization pressure proxy
sources.caveat: Not a drainage model or current street-level building census; use as temporal urbanization indicator.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap
sources.use: Roads, bridges, waterways, drains where mapped, buildings, places, schools, clinics, shelters
sources.caveat: Completeness varies dramatically. Missing OSM feature does not mean real-world absence. ODbL attribution required.

sources.name: Geofabrik Ghana/Cameroon extracts
sources.use: Reproducible bulk OSM ingestion and historical snapshots
sources.caveat: ODbL; check feature schema and snapshot timestamp.

sources.name: HOT Export Tool API
sources.use: Automated filtered exports for flood AOIs / humanitarian mapping projects
sources.caveat: Jobs/authentication required; use Geofabrik for national bulk baselines.

sources.name: Healthsites API v3
sources.use: Clinics/hospitals and health-access exposure layer
sources.caveat: OSM-derived and completeness varies; validate critical facilities locally.

sources.name: geoBoundaries gbOpen
sources.use: Open administrative boundaries for reproducible joins and map layers
sources.caveat: Use gbOpen (CC BY) where possible; compare with official/COD boundaries for operations.

sources.name: OCHA Common Operational Datasets (COD-AB)
sources.use: Humanitarian standard administrative boundaries and place names
sources.caveat: Country edition/version can change; store release ID and checksum.

sources.name: EM-DAT
sources.access: Portal export; archive; HDX country profiles
sources.use: Disaster event seed list, impacts, dates, locations, disaster subtypes
sources.caveat: Living public data is updated weekly; completeness/accuracy caveats and commercial-use/license restrictions are important.

sources.name: GDACS API
sources.use: Event IDs, alerts, bounding boxes, flood AOIs/GFM observed polygons, links to information products
sources.caveat: Alert/event data is operational context; cross-check impact figures before treating as final.

sources.name: ReliefWeb API v2
sources.use: Reports/disasters, GLIDE links, chronology, impact narratives, source documents
sources.caveat: Original reports may be copyrighted; API has quotas. Store metadata/extracted facts + source URL, not indiscriminate content copies.

sources.name: IFRC GO API
sources.use: Emergency events, affected counts, appeals/DREF, situation reports and humanitarian response context
sources.caveat: Event figures evolve; keep retrieval timestamp and source document lineage.

sources.name: GLIDE Number
sources.use: Stable-ish external disaster identifier to join ReliefWeb/IFRC/GDACS/other records
sources.caveat: Not every event/source has GLIDE; use as one identifier among several.

sources.name: Copernicus Marine Global Ocean Physics forecast
sources.use: Sea level, currents and coastal compound-flood context
sources.caveat: ~0.083° global model is regional context, not street-scale storm-surge inundation.

sources.name: Copernicus Marine Global Waves forecast
sources.use: Wave height/period/direction for coastal-flood/erosion compounding
sources.caveat: Regional ocean-wave model; local nearshore transformation/tides still needed.

sources.name: Copernicus Marine ocean/wave reanalysis
sources.use: Historical sea-level/wave context for compound-flood reconstruction
sources.caveat: Product-specific temporal/spatial resolution; use local tide gauges if available.

sources.name: Local municipal engineering records
sources.use: Drain dimensions, culverts, maintenance, blockage, road works, stormwater networks
sources.caveat: Often the most valuable urban-flood data and the least open. Build partnership workflow and confidence tiers.

sources.name: Citizen/field reports
sources.provider: Cameroon DPC / Cameroon Red Cross / councils / community partners
sources.access: Structured field app / hotline/social evidence after governance review
sources.use: Road passability, blocked drains, flood depth photos, facility status and verified community observations
sources.caveat: Needs verification, privacy safeguards, geolocation/time confidence and anti-rumor controls.

sources.name: IoT gauges / rainfall sensors
sources.use: High-frequency local rainfall, water level, drain level and field truth
sources.caveat: Hardware maintenance/calibration and connectivity are major operational risks.
